eligibility_note: Open to international students. Budget NZ$57,300 tuition plus NZ$18,000-22,000/yr Christchurch living - roughly NZ$85,000-95,000 (INR 43-48 lakh) all-in. Christchurch living costs are genuinely 20-25% below Auckland; shared flats in Riccarton/Ilam near campus are common. Honest warning: an MA in humanities is one of the weakest NZ programmes for employment outcomes for an Indian graduate - NZ policy and communications employers strongly favour candidates with NZ work experience and often want work rights or residency. It gives full 3-year PSW, but you will likely spend the first year in unrelated work. Choose it only with a genuine research/PhD ambition or a specific subject (Linguistics, Political Science, Media) connected to a job you have already scoped. The compulsory research methods course is writing-heavy - IELTS 6.5 is the floor, realistically you want 7.0.

eligibility_note: Open to international students. The single best qualification in this batch for an Indian student whose goal is a NZ career and residence, and worth the money in a way the Arts programmes are not. Washington Accord accreditation makes the degree portable back to India or on to Australia/UK/Canada/US. ~NZ$285,000-300,000 all-in over four years (INR 145-155 lakh) - apply for the NZ$15,000 UC International First Year Scholarship and the India-eligible High Achievers award. THE ENTRY BAR IS HIGH AND SPECIFIC: 85% overall in ISC/AISSC plus 60% English, Std XII Maths WITH CALCULUS, Physics and Chemistry (Chemistry waived for Computer/Electrical/Mechatronics/Software). Below 85%? UC Foundation Studies, UCIC and the International Diploma in University Studies are legitimate pathways in. Note the ACCELERATED September route: eligible Indian students can compress the degree to 3.25 years, saving roughly three-quarters of a year of fees. DISCIPLINE CHOICE DETERMINES YOUR RESIDENCE OUTCOME: Civil, Structural, Geotechnical, Mechanical, Electrical, Electronics and Environmental Engineer are Tier 1 Straight to Residence; Software Engineer is also Tier 1; Chemical & Process and Forest Engineering are not. Start lining up the 100 days (800 hours) of placement from year 2. IELTS 6.0/5.5 admits you but engineering reports and group work realistically need 6.5+. NOTE: same qualification as id 363 (UC's official title is 'Bachelor of Engineering with Honours') - the two should be merged.

eligibility_note: Limited international places. UC is unusually explicit that it accepts applications from anyone meeting the admission requirements, including international applicants, so this is not formally closed - but treat it as one of the HARDEST admissions in New Zealand. Only up to 26 places each year against a very large domestic applicant pool, and selection culminates in a Selection Day held in person in Christchurch in November, which is expensive and awkward from India. Two structural hurdles: entry needs a psychology HONOURS degree with abnormal psychology and research methods (a standard three-year Indian B.A./B.Sc. Psychology will not qualify, so most Indian applicants must first complete a NZ postgraduate year or master's, adding a year and NZ$45,000+); and the English bar is IELTS 7.5 overall with nothing below 7.0 - higher than any other programme in this batch and not negotiable. ~NZ$160,000 for the diploma alone before the preparatory year. The reward is real: Clinical Psychologist is Green List Tier 1 with acute shortages. But go in knowing the odds and have a fallback.

The 2-year length is an immigration advantage (two years of 20 hrs/week work rights during study, then a 3-year PSW). Per AUT official page, from 2027 this PGDip is restricted to invited internal AUT master's students; a new Indian applicant cannot enter it directly. Be realistic: an Indian student cannot apply to this directly from India, and from 2027 it becomes invitation-only for AUT's own MHSc Psychology students. The full pathway from an Indian BA/BSc Psychology: AUT BHSc (Honours) Psychology (1 yr, ~NZ$42,000) → MHSc Psychology (2 yrs, ~NZ$90,000) → intern psychologist registration → secure an internship → this diploma (1 yr). That is 4 years, well over NZ$200,000 tuition plus ~NZ$110,000 living, with competitive selection and a hard internship bottleneck at every stage. Two underestimated barriers: internship placements are scarce and NZ providers strongly prefer domestic candidates with local cultural competence including Te Tiriti o Waitangi and Māori and Pacific mental health frameworks; and the English standard (IELTS 7.0 all bands) reflects clinical work demanding fluency far beyond test scores. The destination is excellent - Tier 1 Green List, acute shortage - but understand it as a 4-year, NZ$300,000+ commitment with real attrition risk.

[VERIFIED VIA OFFICIAL AUT SITE, browser, Jul 2026] code AK3558; Level 8; 120 points; 1 year full-time / part-time available; Campus: North Campus; Starts: 22 Feb 2027 | 12 Jul 2027. Structural prerequisite: only open to already-registered NZ nurses who meet prescribing practicum requirements. An Indian student cannot enter this directly on arrival; it is a post-registration upskilling diploma. Be blunt: this is not an entry route to New Zealand. Designed for nurses already registered and practising in NZ, and the one-year-of-NZ-practice requirement plus the need for an employer-provided prescribing mentor makes it structurally unavailable to someone applying from India. AUT publishes an international fee, which is why aggregator sites list it as an 'international course' - ignore that; you will not meet the practicum prerequisites on arrival. The correct sequence for an Indian BSc Nursing graduate: (1) get your qualification assessed by the Nursing Council; (2) meet the Council's English standard - IELTS Academic 7.0 overall with no band below 6.5, or OET grade B, which is HIGHER than AUT's 6.5 entry bar and is where most Indian nurses actually fail; (3) complete a Competence Assessment Programme; (4) register as an RN, work 3+ years, and only then consider RN prescribing.

This is an online (~40 hour) competence-assessment short course run with the NZ Paramedic Council for already-qualified overseas paramedics. Online + short + non-award = no NZ student visa and no post-study work rights. AUT lists this among its health sciences short courses but publishes no public fee or duration page, so the numbers are deliberately null rather than invented. This is the single most useful item in this batch for an ALREADY-QUALIFIED Indian paramedic, because it is the mechanism converting an overseas qualification into NZ registration. Critical sequencing: you do NOT enrol first. You apply to Te Kaunihera Manapou, they assess your overseas qualification, and only if they direct you to a competence assessment do you book it at AUT or Whitireia - self-funded. Be realistic: Indian paramedic/EMT diplomas and BSc Emergency Medical Technology degrees are frequently assessed as not equivalent to the NZ paramedic scope, in which case the Council may require full degree-level study instead. The English bar (Council standard ~IELTS 7.0 with no band below 6.5, or OET B) is higher than any AUT course requirement and is the most common failure point. As a short non-degree course it carries no post-study work rights.

Health Management is a major within the Bachelor of Health Science (parent code AK3680). Open, uncomplicated admission and the same 3-year PSW as the clinical degrees - an easy 'yes' on paper and a harder question in practice. The uncomfortable truth: health MANAGEMENT roles in New Zealand are overwhelmingly filled by people who first worked clinically or who have several years of NZ health-sector experience; a fresh graduate with no NZ work history typically starts in administrative or coordinator roles that may pay BELOW the median wage needed for residence. Three pieces of advice. First, do not treat this as a management degree - treat it as a health-sector entry degree and get a part-time job in a clinic, aged-care facility or hospital administration team from year one, because NZ employers weight local experience heavily. Second, deliberately bolt on quantitative and digital skills (health informatics, data analysis, project management) - that is where the hiring pressure sits. Third, plan the postgraduate step: this degree feeds naturally into the MHSc or a health-management master's, and a Level 9 qualification meaningfully improves both salary and SMC points.

One: as a staged entry into the Master of Gastronomy (id 163), where the 60 points credit forward onto a Level 9 degree with full 3-year work rights - if that is your plan, apply directly to the master's instead, since the entry requirements are barely different apart from the B average. Two: genuine academic interest if you are already in NZ. Entry is easier than the master's (no B grade average specified), a legitimate backup if your bachelor's marks fall short - but confirm in writing that the credit will transfer.

eligibility_note: Limited international places. BY FAR the strongest programme in this batch and one of the best residence pathways in all of New Zealand. Speech Language Therapist is Green List Tier 1 - Straight to Residence - so with an accredited-employer job offer you can apply for residence immediately, no 24-month wait. And unlike most clinical programmes, NO prior NZ registration is needed to enter. Three realities: (1) Cost ~NZ$125,000-130,000 (INR 63-66 lakh) over two years with living. (2) Entry is explicitly LIMITED and competitive - departmental interview, statement of interest, hard 1 October deadline for the February intake ONLY, so a missed deadline costs a full year; start 12+ months ahead. (3) English is the real barrier - IELTS 7.0 with nothing below 6.5, well above UC's normal 6.5/6.0, because you will be assessing and treating NZ clients' speech. Many international SLP students find the clinical placements, not the coursework, the hardest part. The statistics prerequisite trips up Indian arts/commerce graduates - if your BA/BCom had no statistics paper, do one before applying.

eligibility_note: Limited international places. A genuinely world-class niche - Christchurch is the literal gateway city for the US, NZ and Italian Antarctic programmes, and Gateway Antarctica has access no other university can match. But treat it as a specialist research investment, not an immigration strategy. Three hard facts. (1) Entry requires you to ALREADY hold a relevant POSTGRADUATE qualification, so an Indian applicant with only a BSc or B.Tech is NOT eligible - you would need an MSc or equivalent first. (2) The timetable is unusual and unforgiving: applications close 31 MARCH, decisions early September, programme starts JULY - roughly a 15-month lead time. Miss March and you wait a full year. (3) Expensive at ~NZ$88,000 (INR 45 lakh) for twelve months with living. It does confer full 3-year PSW, but the job market is tiny and mostly funded research or government policy roles that favour residents. Check with Gateway Antarctica whether your intake includes an Antarctic field component - any ice deployment carries additional cost and medical clearance. Recommended only for a committed climate/polar researcher heading toward a PhD.

eligibility_note: Open to international students. The flexible, general-purpose engineering Master's - lets you pick from nine endorsements. NOTE THE DURATION RANGE: UC states 1-3 YEARS full-time. Establish upfront whether you are doing a 120-point taught-and-project version in one year or a longer research version, and get the expected completion date in writing. eligibility_note: Limited international places. The delivery model, not the academics, rules this out for most Indian applicants. UC delivers the PGDipCEP EXCLUSIVELY through UC Online as a part-time, two-year programme with about 20 days onsite in Christchurch. Immigration NZ does not grant student visas for online or part-time study, so you cannot use this to move to New Zealand, cannot work part-time while studying, and get no post-study work visa - while still having to fly to Christchurch for the onsite practical blocks on a visitor visa. UC also does not publish an international tuition figure for this diploma - get a written fee quote before doing anything else. The profession itself is small and still establishing in NZ, there is no statutory registration, and it does not appear on the Green List. Realistic use case: an Indian physiotherapist or sport scientist already living in NZ. As a study-abroad plan from India, choose the Master of Audiology (id 300) or the PGDipHealSc (id 319) instead.

eligibility_note: Open to international students. The strongest programme in this batch for an Indian applicant wanting both a real subject and real work prospects. Christchurch is arguably the best place on earth to study disaster resilience - UC rebuilt itself after the 2010-11 earthquakes and the city is a live laboratory with GNS Science, NIWA, EQC and a mature resilience consulting sector on the doorstep. But the price is steep: ~NZ$90,000-95,000 all-in. Two practical tips: first, if your Indian degree included statistics or quantitative methods, say so explicitly - the STAT prerequisite is waivable. Second, much sector work is with government agencies and Crown Research Institutes, which sometimes prefer or require residents for security-sensitive roles, so target private consultancy and insurance risk modelling for your first job. No direct Green List occupation, so residence runs through SMC points or by later adding an engineering credential.

Genuine strengths: it IS a Level 7 degree, so you get the full 3-year PSW and the strongest SMC points base of the sub-degree options; AUT holds UNWTO TedQual certification; and the BA structure lets you combine tourism with marketing, event management, HR or a language, which materially widens employability - do this, a pure tourism BA is narrow. NZ is a genuinely interesting place to study aerospace - one of the highest per-capita rocket launch rates in the world thanks to Rocket Lab, plus Dawn Aerospace and Kea Aerospace, with Canterbury as the national hub. ~NZ$105,000-112,000 total (INR 53-57 lakh) over 18 months. RESIDENCE REALITY CHECK: aerospace and aeronautical engineering are NOT among the Green List Tier 1 occupations NZ names. Many aerospace graduates do work under a Mechanical or Electrical/Electronics Engineer title, which IS Tier 1 - but that depends on the job title your employer puts on the employment agreement, not on your degree. If your priority is a guaranteed residence route, the Master of Civil Engineering or ME with a Mechanical/Electrical endorsement is a safer bet at similar or lower cost.

eligibility_note: Open to international students. Genuinely strong on reputation: UC is ranked 61st in the world for Linguistics in the 2026 QS subject rankings and its New Zealand Institute of Language, Brain and Behaviour is internationally respected for sociophonetics and speech research. One year, Level 9, 180 points, up to 3 years PSW, at a special programme fee CHEAPER than the standard Arts Master's. Two entry traps: first, the bar is B+ in 60 points of 300-level Linguistics - an Indian BA English literature degree will usually NOT satisfy this without the LING400 bridging route; second, LING400 runs over the NZ summer as a distance course, so plan it before your February start. Employability advice: pure linguistics jobs in NZ are scarce, so deliberately steer your thesis and course choices toward computational linguistics, speech technology or corpus/NLP methods - that is where the hiring is, and it converts a humanities Master's into an ICT-adjacent CV with far more traction on a post-study work visa.

eligibility_note: Open to international students. FAR AND AWAY the best financial proposition in the batch and badly underappreciated by Indian students. International PhD candidates pay DOMESTIC tuition rates - around NZ$30,000 TOTAL over three years, against NZ$35,000-50,000 for a taught master's per year. On top of that you can work while studying, your partner can get an open work visa, and dependent children attend school as domestic students. Add a UC Doctoral Scholarship and the degree can be close to cost-neutral. The real currency is not marks but a SUPERVISOR: email potential supervisors with a concrete research proposal 6-12 months ahead - no supervisor means no admission. You can start on the first day of any month. The caution is opportunity cost - 3-4 years is a long time, and humanities PhDs face a thin academic job market in NZ.

data_source: Official University of Canterbury website (individually researched, Jul 2026)
eligibility_note: Limited international places. One of the genuinely attractive options in this batch for an Indian graduate - one year, NZ$34,625 tuition, ending in a registrable, Green-List occupation with real vacancies. The wall is English. The Teaching Council requires IELTS Academic 7.0 with NO band below 7.0, and UC cannot waive it because it is a registration rule. Most Indian applicants who fail do so on writing or speaking. Sit IELTS early - the Teaching Council will let you combine bands across sittings taken within two years. Second point of realism: this is Tier 2, not Tier 1 - a Work to Residence pathway needing 24 months of skilled NZ employment, so plan for roughly three years in NZ before residence. ECE salaries are modest relative to the fee, so payback is slow if borrowing. Confirm the post-study work visa treatment with INZ in writing - it is a Level 7 graduate diploma and only qualifies through the registration exception.

Public-health master's pathway. Level 8 diploma over a full year - PSW-eligible. Two practical warnings. First, taught mainly at South Campus in Manukau, roughly 45-60 minutes by public transport from central Auckland and most student accommodation - either budget for South Auckland flatting or a long daily commute. Second, AUT delivers this via block courses and blended/online learning for domestic students, but your visa forces you into the on-campus offerings, which reduces timetable flexibility and your ability to work the permitted 20 hours. The equity, social justice and Māori health framing is not decoration - assessments expect engagement with Te Tiriti o Waitangi, unfamiliar ground for most Indian applicants and worth reading up on before arrival. Value judgement: NZ$46.5k for a one-year Level 8 diploma with no Green List route and a weak public-sector job market is hard to justify unless you already hold a clinical qualification or intend to progress to the Master of Public Health.

Base Bachelor of Engineering (Honours) (code AK3751) - parent of the civil, construction, electrical, mechanical, mechatronics, architectural engineering majors. Washington-Accord-accredited; engineers on the Green List. Level 8 degree, PSW-eligible - a top residence pathway. The flagship undergraduate engineering option and, for an Indian student who can fund four years, the single best long-term investment in this batch. Budget honestly: ~NZ$196,000 tuition + ~NZ$110,000 Auckland living = NZ$300,000+, and the NZ$5,000-10,000 scholarship covers only a small fraction. Key advice: (1) Physics AND Maths at Std XII are mandatory - the number one rejection reason for Indian applicants; if you lack them, route via the Diploma in Engineering. (2) Washington Accord accreditation means the degree retains full value if you return to India or move to Australia/Canada - this de-risks the investment considerably. (3) Choose your major with the Green List in mind: Civil, Structural and Software have the deepest NZ demand. (4) The IELTS bar (6.0 / 5.5 bands) is unusually accessible for a degree of this calibre, but engineering teamwork and Year 4 industry projects demand real spoken fluency - aim higher than the minimum. (5) Main intake February. (6) Get a NZ driver's licence early.
